Add a bounded real-browser Tab traversal that records focus order, whether the focused element paints an outline or shadow (WCAG 2.4.7), whether focus vanishes while controls are unreached, and whether a short cycle repeats; compose it as a required deep-mode check that is not-run rather than pass when nothing was driven.
acc: a deep audit records Tab order, focus indicators, detours and cycles per route on a real page
a missing focus indicator is a P1 finding that names the element; a detour is P1; a cycle is P2 because Escape is not pressed
quick mode, a missing browser or an undriven page reports keyboard-flow as not-run, never pass
reaching the end of the document is not reported as a detour or a cycle, and the rule is pinned by a test in both directions
the check is declared in the audit contract with its gate, mode, effort and requirement, and the docs state what it does not press
tasks.risk: a traversal that counts wrap-around as a defect invents findings, which is worse than having no check
tasks.rollback: delete the harness, its tests, the contract entry and the compose block; deep audits return to five required checks
tasks.approval: D32 issue triage (issue #13, P1) within D28 build authorization
results: scanKeyboard presses Tab at most 30 times on a 1440x900 page, recording tag+id/classes (never page content), computed outline/box-shadow while focused, body landings and repeat patterns; it opens its own browser context so it cannot disturb the axe page and never throws to the caller

compose turns a missing indicator into a P1 (WCAG 2.4.7) naming the element, a detour into a P1 with expected 0 observed N, and a cycle into a P2 that says an observation was made and Escape was not pressed; with no samples the check is not-run, so quick mode and a missing browser cannot read as pass

the first live run reported a detour and a cycle on fixtures/portfolio and both were the scanner's fault: 30 presses over 9 controls wrap the document and Chromium parks focus on body at the wrap. The definition now separates an end-of-document body stop (every control already reached, truncated, not a finding) from a mid-page one (controls unreached, a real detour), and looks for cycles only in a repeated suffix of period 1-3 before truncation; one test pins the wrap case as clean and another pins the vanishing case as a detour

measured: deep audit of fixtures/portfolio/dist gives keyboard-flow pass with 30 Tab stops recorded, while the same report still fails axe-a11y (P0 scrollable-region-focusable), a 400% zoom overflow and 390 px tap targets, so the check discriminates instead of passing everything

not claimed: Escape dismissal, arrow-key and roving-tabindex semantics, indicator adequacy beyond presence, screen-reader announcements, or any detour beyond the 30-press bound; these are named in AUDIT_WILL_NOT, LIMITATIONS.md and the receipt

tasks.title: A reachable scroll container is not page overflow (issue #13 false-positive rule)
tasks.obj: Issue #13 requires negative fixtures to catch overflow without creating false positives for legitimate scrollable grids. The 400% zoom record counted every leaf wider than the viewport as overflow, so a data grid inside overflow-x:auto would be reported as a defect. Treat auto|scroll ancestors as containment, keep hidden|clip as overflow because hiding is not a fix, and pin all three cases with real-browser tests.
acc: a wide leaf inside an overflow-x auto or scroll ancestor is not reported as page overflow by the zoom record or the matrix
a wide leaf with no scroller is still reported, and overflow-x hidden or clip still counts as overflow
each of the three cases is pinned by a real-browser test, and the docs state the rule
tasks.risk: a containment rule that is too broad silences real overflow, and clipping is the cheapest way to game an overflow check
tasks.rollback: revert the containedByScroller guard and delete the three tests
tasks.approval: D32 issue triage (issue #13, P1) within D28 build authorization
results: metrics.ts now skips a wide leaf when some ancestor between it and body declares overflow-x auto or scroll: the content is reachable and the container is cued, which is containment rather than page overflow

hidden and clip are deliberately not containment: the page stops scrolling while the content stays unreachable, so the leaf is still named, which keeps clipping from being a way to pass the overflow check

measured in a real browser: 900px inside overflow-x:auto gives every matrix cell overflow false, overflowingElements [] and a clean zoom record; 900px with no scroller gives cell overflow true and a zoom record naming the leaf; 900px inside overflow-x:hidden gives quiet matrix cells (the page no longer scrolls) but a zoom record that names the leaf, which is the case a document-level check cannot see

the matrix cell was already correct (it reads documentElement.scrollWidth vs clientWidth); the defect was in the zoom record's OR over overflowingElements, which the audit's reflow-matrix finding cites
not claimed: that a scrolling grid is usable (arrow-key scrollability, affordance and frozen first column are separate checks), nor any special handling of overflow:overlay

tasks.obj: Issue #15 needs a scoped command that audits only a selected element/section and proposes improvements, without a second scanner. Resolve a scope reference (DOM selector, component path, region annotation, editor selection) to stable source/DOM identifiers, detect stale/ambiguous/absent targets and ask for clarification instead of editing something else, and derive a minimal focus set (responsive, a11y, motion, copy, performance, visual) from the component kind so irrelevant checks are reported not-applicable rather than run.

screenshot-only or ambiguous selections are marked advisory and never silently mapped to a different element
the focus set is chosen per component kind and the report lists consulted sources with provenance and not-consulted limitations
tasks.risk: a wrong scope silently edits a component the user did not select
tasks.rollback: keep the audit command as the only entry point; delete the resolver
tasks.approval: D32 issue triage (issue #15) within D28 build authorization
results: resolveScope returns one of five named outcomes (resolved, ambiguous, not-found, advisory, rejected) with separate clarification and reason fields, so a caller never parses prose to decide whether it may proceed; only resolved offers a focus set

an ambiguous selector returns every candidate and focus null instead of picking the first match, a stale selector or unreadable path returns not-found with a reselect instruction, a drawn region is advisory by construction because pixels are not source, and empty, '*', 'html *', over-long and control-character selectors are refused before reaching the browser

descriptors are tag#id.class with id preferred and never inner text, so targets cannot leak page content into a report; selectors only ever reach document.querySelectorAll inside the page, with no shell or eval path

selectFocus partitions all six dimensions for each of seven component classes, with a reason on every exclusion; performance is not-applicable for a single control or generic scope (no scripted interaction is driven) and copy is not-applicable for a record table (content needs a content kind), so neither is dressed up as measured

tasks.title: Best Practice Proposal contract: observed facts vs heuristics, diff, risk, test plan, no mutation
tasks.obj: Produce the proposal the issue specifies: current behaviour, evidence, why it is suboptimal, remedy and rationale, affected source/DOM locations, expected UX outcome, risk and regression surface, before/after diff and test plan, severity-ranked, with observed facts separated from heuristic recommendations and untested dimensions listed. Read-only by default: writing a proposal must mutate nothing, and applying it must require explicit per-hunk approval in the existing Live Studio approval flow.
acc: a proposal is emitted as a validated record with facts separated from heuristics, and no file changes when only the proposal mode runs
approval is required per hunk before any write, and undoing an applied proposal restores the previous bytes exactly
a malicious page or MCP reference cannot widen approval scope; the policy is tested
tasks.risk: a proposal path that writes without approval turns a read-only command into an unattended editor
tasks.rollback: proposal files stay on disk as evidence; revert the writer and keep the plan artifact
tasks.approval: D32 issue triage (issue #15) within D28 build authorization
results: BestPracticeProposal (sus.bestpractice-proposal/1) is Zod-validated before it exists: every item carries dimension, severity, kind, title, location, evidence, observed, expected, why, remedy, rationale, uxOutcome, risk and a testPlan with at least one step

two invariants are schema-enforced rather than documented: a fact without observed plus evidence is refused (fact-without-observation), and a heuristic ranked P0/P1 is refused (heuristic-ranked-blocking), so an unmeasured opinion can neither be built nor ranked as blocking

composeProposal refuses an unresolved scope (ambiguous, not-found, advisory or rejected) quoting the clarifier, and refuses an empty item list as no-items; sorting is worst-first with measured facts before judgment at equal severity

the record carries a SHA-256 digest over canonically serialised scope, focus, items and untested, and authoriseApply refuses empty approval, a stale digest (content edited after approval), a hunk absent from the proposal, and a change in a dimension listed as untested, allowing only a matching digest with known hunks on measured dimensions

untested dimensions are copied from the scope's not-applicable list with their reasons and any measured-but-open dimension is merged rather than dropped (both facts are kept), and the rendered report always ends with a Not measured section

read-only is structural: the module imports no filesystem writer, and a test lists a temp directory before and after composeProposal and requires it identical; applying stays in Studio's T0707 path (content-bound grant, preimage hash recheck, byte-exact rollback) rather than a second writer

markdown output escapes every '<', '>', '&', '|', '*', '_', '[', ']' and backslash in page-derived text, so a title cannot inject report structure; the test inspects escaping rather than substrings because a backslash-escaped tag still contains the tag text
20 tests pass with no browser and no I/O; pnpm verify 0
not claimed: no diff or patch is generated, no command routes sus.bestpractice yet (T1023), this module measures nothing itself, and rollback semantics are T0707's and are cited rather than re-tested

tasks.title: T1003-6 (medium) — recovery honors the same containment, and 'missing' cannot masquerade as a hash
tasks.obj: Transaction.apply/recover executed manifest file paths with no containment check, so a planted prepared manifest could write or delete outside the root on the next recovery; the conflict classifier compared the literal sentinel 'missing' against stored preimageSha256, so a manifest declaring 'missing' defeated the check.
